articles.title: Cómo tener un Cybercab de Elon Musk, el robotaxi sin pedales que ya está operando
articles.text:
Tesla abrió el registro para personas y empresas que busquen formar parte de su red de Cybercab, el robotaxi sin volante ni pedales. El formulario es, por ahora, el único paso público para quienes quieran adquirir una flota o colaborar con la infraestructura del servicio.
Este proceso tiene el objetivo de empezar la expansión de Tesla en el transporte autónomo y ser un modelo en el que propietarios puedan prestar sus vehículos para realizar viajes. Por ahora, el Cybercab ya opera comercialmente en Austin, Texas, mientras la autoridad federal revisa cómo fue certificado.
PUBLICIDAD
El formulario para quienes quieran tener un Cybercab de Tesla
Tesla habilitó una inscripción para quienes estén interesados en participar en su futura red de robotaxis. El trámite pide nombre, teléfono, correo electrónico y la región en la que el solicitante planea desplegar los vehículos.
La compañía también consulta qué tipo de vínculo busca cada interesado. Las opciones contemplan la adquisición de una flota de Cybercab o la participación en centros de movilidad e infraestructura necesarios para el funcionamiento del servicio.
PUBLICIDAD
El formulario invita a colaborar con la construcción de la red de robotaxis de Tesla. Sin embargo, no establece todavía las condiciones comerciales que deberán cumplir los potenciales operadores.
No se conoce si será necesario comprometer una cantidad mínima de vehículos para acceder a una flota. Tesla tampoco informó si venderá los Cybercab directamente, si los entregará mediante alquiler o si propondrá una asociación para operar unidades dentro de su plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD
Por ahora, quien pretenda tener un Cybercab debe completar el registro, elegir la región de despliegue e indicar si busca una flota o un papel vinculado con la infraestructura. La empresa no difundió precios, plazos de entrega, requisitos técnicos ni contratos.
Cómo es el modelo de alquiler que plantea Elon Musk
La propuesta de Tesla no se limita a vender vehículos. Elon Musk ha explicado que los propietarios podrían incorporar sus Cybercab a una red de robotaxis cuando no los estén utilizando.
PUBLICIDAD
La idea consiste en que esos automóviles realicen viajes de pasajeros de manera autónoma y generen ingresos para sus dueños. Tesla pondría a disposición elementos de su infraestructura, entre ellos su aplicación y servicios de localización.
Musk comparó el modelo con una combinación entre Airbnb y Uber. La fórmula apunta a que una persona use su vehículo cuando lo necesite y lo ponga a trabajar dentro de la plataforma durante los momentos en que esté disponible.
PUBLICIDAD
El dueño no tendría que conducirlo. El Cybercab fue concebido para trasladar pasajeros sin intervención humana, por lo que su función en la red sería realizar trayectos bajo el control del sistema autónomo.
Musk sostuvo que algunos clientes podrían conseguir más dinero por prestar el vehículo a la flota de lo que les cuesta arrendarlo a Tesla. “Te pagan por tener un Tesla”, afirmó al describir esa posibilidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Tesla no explicó cómo se repartirán los ingresos entre la compañía y los propietarios. Tampoco definió si el interesado podrá comprar el robotaxi, arrendarlo o gestionarlo mediante un convenio.
Cómo es el Cybercab y su funcionamiento
El Cybercab es un vehículo creado desde cero para operar como taxi autónomo. No tiene volante ni pedales, de modo que ningún conductor ni pasajero puede tomar el control físico durante un recorrido.
PUBLICIDAD
Tesla sostiene que el sistema autónomo toma todas las decisiones de conducción. Esa condición diferencia al Cybercab de otros robotaxis que utilizan automóviles convencionales adaptados con tecnología de conducción autónoma.
En esos modelos adaptados, el vehículo conserva mandos manuales aunque el sistema pueda conducir. El Cybercab elimina esos componentes desde su concepción y se destina exclusivamente al transporte sin conductor humano.
PUBLICIDAD
El modelo comenzó recientemente su operación comercial en Austin, Texas. Antes de ese despliegue, Tesla ya ofrecía viajes autónomos en la ciudad mediante unidades del Model Y.
Luego amplió sus operaciones a otras ciudades de Texas, Florida y California. En varios de esos mercados, las normas estatales exigen que los vehículos autónomos tengan un supervisor humano capaz de asumir la conducción.
Por qué la NHTSA investiga a Tesla
La NHTSA investiga cómo Tesla certificó que el Cybercab cumple las normas federales de seguridad. La revisión se centra en que el robotaxi no tiene volante ni pedales, elementos exigidos para ciertos vehículos comerciales salvo que exista una exención.
Según el regulador, Tesla no solicitó ese permiso. La pesquisa no declara inseguro al modelo ni establece un incumplimiento definitivo: busca evaluar el proceso y los datos técnicos utilizados por la empresa. El caso surgió tras el inicio de operaciones en Austin, Texas, donde Tesla tiene 314 robotaxis registrados, incluidos 45 Cybercab.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Vigilant app raises questions about cycle of duplicate platforms
articles.text:
On September 1, the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) launched the Vigilant App, a digital platform that allows Nigerians to report suspected financial fraud, upload evidence, track their cases and receive feedback.
The Force’s Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Department developed the app with stakeholders across the financial sector. The police say the platform is designed to improve how financial fraud is reported and how cases are handled with relevant institutions.
Olatunji Disu, the Inspector-General of police (IGP), described the app as part of the Force’s digital transformation. “The policing environment is changing rapidly. Crime is becoming more sophisticated, information moves faster, and citizens increasingly expect public institutions to be accessible and responsive to technology. The Nigeria police Force must, therefore, evolve with these realities.”
That sounds straightforward. But Vigilant is not entering an empty system.
We’ve been here before with the police
The police have spent years trying to use digital platforms to make it easier for Nigerians to report crimes. In 2017, the police launched Hawk Eye, an anonymous crime-reporting platform that allowed Nigerians to send information through video, voice or text. Lagos-based ICT firm Web Assets Nigeria Limited, along with other technology partners, developed the system. It was initially piloted in the Federal Capital Territory, with plans to expand to Lagos and other states.
The police said patrol vehicles equipped with mobile terminals would receive reports from a command-and-control centre for quicker responses. But by 2019, TechCabal reported that Hawk Eye had largely become defunct, raising an early example of what happens when a Police technology initiative does not survive beyond its initial rollout.
In 2021, the Force introduced Rescue Me, another platform designed to connect Nigerians to the Police Command and Control unit during emergencies and to allow them to report crimes. The app offers emergency alerts, crime reporting, reporting police officers, navigation, and ambulance requests. The Police said it was designed to facilitate rapid responses to crimes and emergencies. The app currently has more than 100,000 downloads on Google Play.
HumAngle reported in 2022 that users had already registered on the platform, although some raised concerns about how much personal information it requested. The Police defended the data collection, saying the information was needed to assist and that access to users’ photos could help identify people in danger.
The platform has also had to deal with a high volume of alerts. In March 2022, the Police said it had received more than 10,000 fake emergency alerts through Rescue Me, which created traffic on the platform and affected genuine callers.
I also downloaded the app to test the registration process. I requested an OTP three times, and as of the time of writing, I have yet to receive one.
Rescue Me, therefore, is not simply another Police app that was launched and forgotten. It has users, remains available and has been used to send emergency alerts. But its history also shows that a digital reporting channel is only one part of the response system.
The police also have a dedicated National Cybercrime Centre (NCCC) reporting system. Its current portal allows people to submit cybercrime reports, upload evidence and track cases. The NCCC describes the system as an end-to-end cybercrime investigation and victim-support platform operating 24/7 across all 36 states. It currently reports more than 146,000 reports filed and more than ₦58 billion in recovered assets.
That makes the NCCC more than just another historical police app. It is an existing system that already provides some of the functions Vigilant is introducing.
Nigerians already have places to report fraud
By a conservative count, Vigilant is at least the fourth citizen-facing reporting platform the police have introduced in under a decade.
None of this means Vigilant is destined to repeat that history. But it does mean the value of the new app has to be measured by more than whether Nigerians can submit a complaint from their phones. For financial fraud, the police are also not the only institution Nigerians can turn to.
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), for example, has Eagle Eye, an online reporting platform designed to ease the reporting of economic and financial crimes. When it launched in July 2021, then-EFCC chairman Abdulrasheed Bawa described it as the first application of its kind by a Nigerian law-enforcement agency. The EFCC later said the platform was producing a steady stream of intelligence and had become a springboard for several investigations. The agency has continued to maintain the platform, which allows users to submit reports and upload evidence.
Banks are another part of the system. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has required financial institutions to maintain fraud desks since 2015, giving customers a direct channel to report suspected fraud. Banks also participate in the Nigeria Electronic Fraud Forum (NeFF), which the CBN established to improve information sharing on electronic fraud across the financial industry.
NIBSS operates an Industry Fraud Reporting Portal through which financial institutions submit and share fraud information. But participation has not been universal. In 2023, NIBSS said only 60 of 163 profiled financial institutions submitted fraud data through the portal.
The CBN has also continued to tighten expectations for financial institutions. In January 2026, it said banks had agreed, through the Nigeria Electronic Fraud Forum, to reduce fraud response times to under 30 minutes as part of efforts to curb electronic fraud. The target was presented as a way to improve the chances of tracing and recovering stolen funds, although the CBN has not yet published industry-wide data showing whether banks have consistently met it.
For customers, the CBN advises those who suspect they have been victims of fraud to contact their financial institution immediately so it can freeze affected accounts and attempt to reverse unauthorised transactions.
This means Vigilant is entering a system where fraud can already be reported to banks, shared across financial institutions, and reported to law-enforcement agencies.
The more interesting question is, what happens after the report? That matters because Nigeria’s fraud problem is not simply about victims having nowhere to complain.
In 2025, digital payment fraud losses fell to ₦25.85 billion ($17.2 million) from ₦52.26 billion ($34.8 million) in 2024, according to NIBSS. But the organisation also said fraud reporting declined by 34% in the fourth quarter of 2025. NIBSS has warned that unreported fraud makes it harder to track and investigate cases.
Getting people to report fraud remains important. But once a report is made, the speed at which information moves among the victim, the financial institution, and law enforcement can determine whether money can still be traced or recovered.
The problems that follow a fraud report
In September 2025, the Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU) held a meeting with the CBN, Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), NIBSS, banks, and fintech companies to discuss fraud investigations. CP Rose Chollom Dung, then Commissioner of Police of the PSFU, identified several problems affecting investigations, including delays in responding to official requests, bureaucratic bottlenecks during urgent situations, inadequate real-time information sharing, and gaps in inter-agency collaboration. The Unit said these problems affected the efficiency and effectiveness of fraud investigations, pointing to a problem beyond reporting.
A victim may already have reported a fraudulent transaction to their bank. The bank may have information about where the money went. The police may need that information to investigate or trace the funds. Other financial institutions may need to act quickly.
If those institutions do not share information quickly enough, does a new platform to submit the original complaint necessarily solve the problem?
So what does Vigilant actually add?
The police’s answer appears to be coordination. The Force says it was developed with financial-sector stakeholders and is intended to support coordination with relevant institutions. But those basic functions are not entirely new within the police.
The NCCC already allows Nigerians to report cybercrime, submit evidence, and track cases. Its current platform states that investigators can handle cybercrime cases, conduct digital forensics, and support victims. So reporting, evidence submission, and case tracking do not, on their own, explain why Vigilant is needed.
The more significant difference is its stated connection to the financial sector. The app’s Google Play listing describes Vigilant as a real-time fraud intelligence, post-transaction tracing, and rapid recovery platform for banks, fintechs, telecommunications companies, insurers, and corporates.
If that integration works as intended, Vigilant could address a weakness in the existing fraud-response system.
But the public information around the launch does not yet show exactly how that coordination works in practice. It does not, for example, establish how quickly a report is routed to a bank, whether a report can trigger an immediate response from a financial institution, or how the police will measure response times through the platform.
I reached out to a source in the Police for clarification on how the platform connects with financial institutions and how reports are handled after submission, but the source declined to comment.
The ability to track a case is useful, but tracking is not the same as resolving it. The NCCC already offers case tracking. The ability to report from a phone is useful, but Nigerians already have several digital reporting channels.
Vigilant’s strongest case, therefore, is not that it gives Nigerians another place to complain. It is that it could make the handoff between the victim, banks, and law enforcement faster and more coordinated.
Another police initiative?
When it comes to police tech initiatives, a question of continuity arises. Sources within the police force who preferred to remain anonymous expressed little confidence in the Vigilant app and told TechCabal they hadn’t heard of it.
The concern is not necessarily that the police should stop building technology. It is about whether every new administration needs another platform when some existing systems already perform parts of the same job.
That concern is especially relevant because the police have already identified delays, information-sharing problems, and inter-agency bottlenecks as obstacles to fraud investigations.
A new app can make reporting easier. It cannot, by itself, make a bank respond faster, make an investigator act faster, or remove bureaucratic bottlenecks.
Vigilant does fill a possible gap, but it is not the access gap. Nigerians already have places to report fraud. Its real value will be determined by what happens after the report is submitted.
If Vigilant can connect victims, banks, and investigators quickly enough to improve tracing, response, and recovery, then the police will have added something meaningful to Nigeria’s fraud-response system. However, if the process after the report remains slow, another reporting platform will have changed the front door without changing what happens behind it.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Xiaomi dévoile le Xiaomi 18 Fold : son rival du Galaxy Z Fold 8 et de l'iPhone pliant — Frandroid
articles.text:
Et voici le troisième combattant dans l’arène, ou bien est-ce le deuxième ? Après le Galaxy Z Fold 8 de Samsung cet été, et avant la présentation attendue de l’iPhone pliant, Xiaomi dévoile ce lundi 7 septembre son premier smartphone pliant avec un format « passeport ».
Voici le Xiaomi 18 Fold. La marque le présente dans son coloris rouge bordeaux, qui devrait être la couleur phare de l’iPhone 18 Pro d’Apple.
Xiaomi ne copie pas la recette Apple et Samsung
Contrairement à Apple et Samsung, Xiaomi semble s’être fixé pour objectif de ne pas faire de concessions sur les caractéristiques de son pliant.
L’essentiel à prix plancher ! Avec l’offre B&You Pure fibre de Bouygues Telecom, profitez du Wi-Fi 7 ultra-rapide (2 Gb/s) sans TV, pour seulement 24,99 €/mois et jusqu’à 148€ offerts* !
Cela se voit notamment par l’appareil photo au dos du smartphone, un module à trois appareils là où la concurrence fait l’impasse sur le téléobjectif. Le triple système Leica repose sur un capteur principal de 200 mégapixels (1/1,56, f/1,7), un téléobjectif 3,5x de 50 mégapixels (1/2,75, f/2,8) et un ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels (1/2,88, f/2,4).
Le Xiaomi 18 Fold intègre une batterie de 6000 mAh, contre 4800 seulement chez Samsung, avec un charge jusqu’à 67W en filaire et 50W en sans-fil.
La puce SoC est la nouvelle Xiaomi Xring O3 très haut de gamme dévoilée quelques jours auparavant.
Un accent sur la fiabilité
Durant la présentation du smartphone, Xiaomi a passé de longues minutes à vanter la fiabilité de son système pliable. La marque affirme s’être fixé pour objectif de coller à la fiabilité des smartphones classiques.
Pour cela, la marque a simulé plus de 253 angles de chute dans trois états : plié, déplié et un angle intermédiaire. En tout, Xiaomi dit avoir réalisé plus de 80 000 tests de chute pour optimiser 492 aspects de la conception du produit.
Le Xiaomi 18 Fold est protégé par du verre UTG, pour Ultra Thin Glass, déjà vu chez Samsung et Google.
Lancement en Chine
Le Xiaomi 18 Fold est pour le moment annoncé en Chine avec un prix débutant à 10 999 yuans (environ 1 400 euros HT) pour 256 Go et 12 Go de RAM.
Xiaomi propose aussi des configurations avec 512 Go et 1 To de stockage, et jusqu’à 16 Go de RAM.

articles.title: China is preparing humanoid robots for combat as researchers push them from labs to the battlefield
articles.text:
Forward-looking: Back when humanoid robots could barely stumble forward without falling over, there were plenty of jokes about their use on the battlefield, Terminator-style, not being much of a concern. Now, though, these machines are running faster than the fastest human and doing parkour – and China wants to turn them into robotic miltary "combatants."
August saw the World Humanoid Robot Games take place in China, where robots took parts in several events. The same month, Unitree claimed its Superman robot can run faster than Usain Bolt, although the figure has not been independently verified.
 – Unitree (@UnitreeRobotics) August 17, 2026
Reuters reports that two days after the Games ended, the People's Liberation Army's official newspaper, the PLA Daily, called for researchers to accelerate the transfer of these technologies from laboratories to military training grounds.
Reuters reviewed more than 100 Chinese military procurement notices, academic studies, patents, official publications, government records, and defense-company materials. It found that the country is accelerating research into the robots' military uses and planning for their eventual wartime deployment.
China has long led the world when it comes to humanoid robots. Its manufacturers accounted for about 95% of shipments of these bots in 2025, giving the PLA plenty of access to the machines.
The good news is that while humanoid robots have come a long way since those slow, lumbering, ungainly early efforts that required a tethered connection to operators, we really are still a long way from seeing squads of marauding T-800 killbots marching across fields. They require a lot of energy, so can't operate for great lengths of time, and even the most advanced designs occasionally fall over, especially on rough terrain.
Robot powered by Qualcomm's new AI chip dies mid-presentation
by u/SuggestionMission516 in singularity
However, China still has plans for how to use humanoid robots. It envisions them being used alongside robot dogs – something that ICE could soon use – and unmanned vehicles, an area that is becoming increasingly popular among global militaries.
In a scenario described by a research paper last year, six combat robots – a mixture of humanoids, robot dogs, and unmanned vehicles – would be split up between two assault teams. Working with ground troops, the robots would clear an enemy-occupied building, floor by floor and room by room. The authors believe the equipment to make this a reality will be ready in 5 to 10 years.
Other proposed uses include reconnaissance, logistics, patrols, and operations inside tunnels and ships. State-owned defense company Norinco says its Fuxi humanoid can carry out sentry duties and all-weather reconnaissance, though it can also be remotely controlled instead of operating autonomously.
There's also the important question of whether a machine can reliably distinguish combatants from civilians or recognize when someone is surrendering. China's defense ministry said in March that AI-powered weapons should remain under human control, though that might bring little assurance to skeptics.
Reuters found no evidence that an armed humanoid has been deployed with an operational PLA unit, but one Chinese military researcher warned that, once the remaining technical and cost barriers are overcome, humanoid robots will "stream onto the battlefield."

articles.title: How Figma Uses AI Agents for Security
articles.text:
The engineering team at software company Figma recently documented how they built AI agents to help their security team investigate alerts, search past incidents, check company systems, and even prepare code fixes. The agents learn from previous investigations, reducing repetitive work and helping engineers resolve complex alerts about 70% faster, while human review and strict controls remain in place.
Source: Figma blog
The team describes a security system built on Panther SIEM that investigates alerts and checks audit logs across AWS, Okta, GitHub, GCP, and osquery, an open-source tool that lets you query computers for security and system information using SQL. It queries more than 100 other sources and can open PRs.
The authors report that this reduced resolution time by about 70% for complex alerts and reduced on-call pages by 20% by lowering the severity of some alerts. Matthew Sullivan, formerly a security engineer at Figma and now at Nition, and Brad Girardeau, security engineering manager at Figma, write:
The alert triage agent (using a model like Claude Opus) is where most of the investigation happens. It receives the full Slack thread history as context, its own steering memory (more on this later), and a set of tools scoped to what a security on-call engineer typically needs during triage.
According to the article, the agentic system uses AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Amazon Kendra, Tines, and a Snowflake-based tool to search historical alerts and investigate Panther data. Sullivan and Girardeau add:
Memory ended up being the thing that had the most impact on how useful the system became over time. We have several kinds, and keeping them separate turned out to be important.
Three types of memory help the system improve investigations over time: past alerts, behavioral guidance, and learned database structures. Safety controls are built into the tools themselves, with agent-created PRs set to draft by default and prompts designed to prevent sensitive data from being shared in public Slack channels.
In the separate article "How Figma stays ahead of vulnerabilities with agents," the engineering team reported that its agents found more than 100 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws missed by traditional tools, and that its code reviewer reached 80% precision within a month. The system also improved detection of known bugs by about 30% through a second review step and the team reported about a 50% reduction in some coding errors after adding automated guidance. While the authors describe the steps they performed to achieve those improvements, they warn:
We can't tell you exactly what to do: The specifics depend on your company size, the risks you face, and the feedback loops you already run. But one main lesson is to improve precision before recall. The order is counterintuitive, because the historical bugs you already have can only measure recall; they barely help with the precision you must fix first.
As security teams give AI agents more responsibility, the role of human approval remains an open question. Cloud security company Wiz recently reporte in "GhostApproval: A Trust Boundary Gap in AI Coding Assistants" that six AI coding assistants could be tricked by malicious repositories while showing users a harmless-looking approval prompt. InfoQ recently covered OpenAI's disclosure regarding sandbox escapes.
Figma acknowledges that the existing AI agents are not perfect, but neither are humans, and concludes that the choice is not between the two, with the right balance between automation and human oversight still evolving.

articles.title: Lo nuevo Google Fotos es una maravilla: ya puedes probarte tus propios outfits con IA
articles.text:
Hace tiempo que Google Fotos dejó de ser solo una app para guardar fotografías y vídeos en la nube. Actualmente tiene decenas de funciones muy útiles, pero nada comparado con lo que acaba de lanzar. La gran G ya ha activado una opción en la que llevaba meses trabajando: el Armario Virtual. Y, tal y como indica su nombre, se trata de un armario online con el que puedes ver toda la ropa que tienes, organizarla y, además, utilizar la IA para crear nuevos conjuntos y ver cómo te quedaría un outfit concreto.
No solo suena impresionante: lo es. De hecho, utilizarlo es tan sencillo que parece mentira. No tienes que hacer nada: la propia app de Google Fotos se encarga de analizar tus fotografías, hacer un inventario de toda la ropa que tienes en tus imágenes y guardarlas en el Armario Virtual. Todo, sin que tengas que hacer absolutamente ningún paso de forma manual.
Todos tus modelos de zapatillas, ropa de deporte, chaquetas, abrigos, camisetas... Todo se almacena perfectamente etiquetado en el armario online. ¿Para qué? Es ahora cuando viene la mejor parte: Google Fotos puede utilizar la IA para crear imágenes de ti mismo con tu ropa. ¿La gracia? A partir de ahora podrás probarte outfits con tu propia ropa desde el móvil.
¿Quieres saber cómo te quedaría el pantalón vaquero azul con la camiseta de Adidas y las zapatillas New Balance? Solo tienes que pedirle a la IA que cree un outfit con esas tres prendas y en cuestión de segundos podrás saber cómo quedan en tu cuerpo. Además, gracias a la potencia de Gemini, es posible reestructurar el prompt para pedirle que cambie la iluminación o ciertos detalles.
Y una cosa más. Google Fotos no solo podrá vestirte virtualmente con tus propias prendas, sino que utilizará el Armario Virtual para analizar qué ropa tienes y recomendarte outfits que pueden quedarte bien. No solo te dirá "ponte esto y esto", sino que te mostrará una foto de cómo queda sin que tú se lo pidas para que sea más fácil descubrir posibles conjuntos que todavía no habías probado.
Una buena y una mala noticia sobre esta función de Google Fotos
Primero la buena. Esta opción de Armario Virtual es totalmente gratuita para los usuarios de Google Fotos. No es necesario pagar nada extra ni estar suscrito a las opciones de pago. La función está apareciendo ya para algunos usuarios y utilizarla es tan fácil como entrar en la sección dedicada y esperar a que analice tu galería.
Ahora lo malo. Por ahora, solo está disponible en Estados Unidos. Google Fotos no ha indicado cuándo se desplegará en el resto del mundo, por lo que toca esperar.

articles.title: Sales of CD and vinyl music sees strong resurgence amid physical media backlash — US sales of ‘retro media’ were up 59% and 18%, respectively, in H1 2026
articles.text:
Sales of CD and vinyl music sees strong resurgence amid physical media backlash — US sales of ‘retro media’ were up 59% and 18%, respectively, in H1 2026
All part of a ‘healthy, diversified marketplace’ including digital, reckons RIAA research VP.
There was good news for the U.S. recorded music industry this week, as the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) announced revenues outpaced inflation in H1 2026. “U.S. recorded music revenue reached $6B in the first half of 2026, up 6.9%,” noted the association. Probably more interesting, though, is that consumers have been seriously splashing cash on retro or legacy physical audio formats. A strong resurgence in CD and vinyl music sales saw both up double figures in the latest figures. “Physical revenues jumped 25.9%, powered by 17.7% vinyl growth and a 58.6% increase in CDs,” reported the RIAA.
With the extremely strong headline growth in ‘retro’ formats, one could be excused for thinking consumers are pulling back from digital music distributors like Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, and so on. However, the RIAA underlines that “every major revenue category grew, reflecting a healthy and increasingly diversified marketplace.” While we focus on streaming, this digital segment generated $4.9B in H1 2026, up 4.7% and remaining the largest source of recorded music industry revenue. Other digital stats worth highlighting are the 6.4% growth in paid subscriptions, reaching $3.4B, and the 3.7% growth in free streaming, reaching $900M.
Returning to physical music media, the RIAA characterizes this resurgence as “continued fan excitement with different ways to experience music across an increasingly varied marketplace.” Indeed, I have seen more and more tempting special edition re-releases and remasters on CD and vinyl, for bands I enjoy listening to.
Overall, the numbers do seem to suggest that the boom in physical music distribution isn’t conclusive evidence that consumers are rejecting how the music streaming industry is changing its offerings (pricing, catalogs, etc). However, there may indeed be some backlash here, as we have seen in the TV/movie streaming business. Some consumers are increasingly frustrated with video streaming offerings and are building up home media catalogs by purchasing DVDs, Blu-rays, etc. We’ve started to see a bit of this in video gaming, too, as the high-profile case regarding Sony PlayStation digital game ownership has stirred some gamers into action.

articles.title: Swiss startup Jaipur Robotics raises €4.3 million to expand its AI operating system across more waste-to-energy plants | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Jaipur Robotics, the Swiss AI company transforming waste plant operations with computer vision and automation, today announced a €4.3 million Seed funding round to pursue market leadership, expand into new regions, and further verticalise and broaden the product depth.
The round was led by EquityPitcher Ventures and High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF). In March 2025, the company announced the successful closing of a €725k pre-Seed funding round led by TiVentures SA, and a few months later, it secured an additional €161k from Venture Kick.
“We envision a future where data from waste fully drives safety and automation. This round enables us to revolutionise entire plant operations,” Ermes Zamboni, co-founder and CEO of Jaipur Robotics.
Founded in 2024 by Ermes Zamboni and Nikhil Prakash, Jaipur Robotics develops computer vision and AI solutions for industrial sites, including Waste-to-Energy (WtE), cement, and biomass plants, making them safer, smarter, and more efficient.
According to the company, WtE plants convert non-recyclable waste into energy, but they face several operational challenges, including the presence of hazardous objects (e.g., gas cylinders, concrete blocks) that can cause costly shutdowns, difficulties in ensuring optimal combustion due to the variability of waste materials, and a shortage of specialised operators to oversee and manage the waste bunkers.
Through its products, the company offers oversized and dangerous item detection in bunkers and truck unloading bays, calorific value mapping (Lower Heating Value – LHV) of waste. Its technology leverages deep learning algorithms and computer vision to enable crane operators to effectively mix waste before it is introduced into the combustion chambers. Operators receive clear, real-time visual guidance through an intuitive heat map that accurately highlights areas of higher and lower calorific values within the bunker.
The company also offers crane-tracking solutions that provide precise, real-time monitoring and prediction of the position and operational status of one or more overhead cranes within the bunker of a Waste-to-Energy plant.
Highlighting its impact, the company reported the following results, calculated per plant per year:
- More than 80% fewer unplanned shutdowns via real-time hazard detection.
- Over €1 million in added value from improved waste mixing as calorific-value mapping optimises combustion and compliance.
- Smarter crane operations with predictive guidance automating crane control and maximising productivity.
With the largest European WtE dataset, comprising over 50 million labelled images, Jaipur Robotics’ system analyses more than 5 million tonnes of waste per year and detects hazardous materials with 99% accuracy.
Anna Stetter, Investment Manager at HTGF, said, “What convinced us to co-lead this round is the combination of a dataset, a founding team with rare depth across mechanical engineering, deep learning, and industrial deployment, and outstanding, measurable results at customer sites.”
Headquartered at Technopole Ticino in Manno, near Lugano, Switzerland, the company has a 40-person team and two R&D centres in Switzerland and Asia. It is actively growing its team across AI, engineering, and commercial roles.

articles.title: Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
articles.text:
Thanks to their ability to provide a smooth ride and quiet powertrain with ease, electric vehicles are a true shoo-in for the high-end luxury automotive segment. Rolls-Royce has the Spectre, Cadillac’s Celestiq is taking bespoke to a whole new level, and Mercedes has given the EQS the full Maybach treatment. From Volkswagen Auto Group, Bentley is just about to debut its 2027 Torcal, a spacious SUV that shares a platform with the electrified Porsche Cayenne.
Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
The British automaker is on the hunt for a new demographic with its first electric vehicle.
I recently got a quick ride in a heavily camouflaged preproduction Torcal as a way to experience it before its official debut toward the end of this month. Between this brute’s spacious interior, supple ride quality, and focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, all signs point to it not just being a viable competitor in the segment, but also characteristically Bentley.
When I say heavily camouflaged, this not only covers (pun intended) the Torcal’s exterior, but the interior as well. Thick black cloth was draped over most of it, to the point of the engineers punching holes in the cloth for proper seatbelt usage. The exterior was rather deceiving, too; apparently they affixed false body paneling under the wrap so as not to fully spoil its overall shape and profile. Upon first glance, it seemed like Bentley took a page from Lucid’s Gravity by making it wider at the front than at the back—in the name of teardrop-resembling aerodynamics—but Martin Page, the Torcal’s product line director-slash-chauffeur for my ride, assured me that what I was seeing (or rather, trying to see) wouldn’t be production.
However, this enabled me to zero in closer on what I could feel and hear. Whether up front or in back, the Torcal is amply spacious, even though it’s noticeably smaller in size and shape than Bentley’s current Bentayga. Page explained the great lengths that engineers reached to ensure it had an isolating and tremendously smooth ride. Running off-the-shelf two-chamber air suspension — common in the rest of the brand’s lineup — would seemingly suffice with an EV’s inherently good chassis balance, but engineers took it a step further by carefully altering the flow of oil through its adaptive dampers. This means that the jump in ride and handling between Comfort and Sport modes is much more discernible. No matter the mode, it rode incredibly smoothly. Heavy focus was paid to the Torcal’s alignment, too, with steering that returns to and maintains center as confidently as possible.
Diving deeper into signature Bentley characteristics, developing the best simulated engine note was high on the list of priorities. Inspiration came from the brand’s V8-powered Turbo R of the 1980s, except the track itself was recorded by a musician’s drum beat and mixed accordingly, rather than simply churned out from a synthesizer.
“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects,” Page shared.
“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects.”
— Martin Page, Torcal’s product line director
The reasoning behind this lies in hearing subtle imperfections, much like one would from an analogue internal combustion powertrain. Going one step further, the Torcal’s throttle tuning seemed to mimic a torquey V8 with progressive power delivery. In light of this, Page added that with this sound turned on, it gives occupants auditory cues to tie to the vehicle’s torque delivery, which is known to help reduce motion sickness. The sound has not yet been finalized and is still being finely tweaked at the time of this writing.
I got a peek at the digital instrument cluster and center infotainment screen — Page had to observe the speed limit, after all. The image these display in the background is of a fine crystal decanter hand-cut by Cumbria Crystal with light shone through it. In Page’s words, this shows the natural refractions and reflections that you get from every one of the cuts. It’s another indication of the brand’s focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, albeit a subtle one.
It’s also worth pointing out that Bentley takes net environmental impact seriously. “In this car we take sustainability to another level, we have clear targets for circular material and green aluminum,” Page shared. “The door cards are made with a natural fiber — not injection-molded plastic — that’s fully recyclable and fully sustainable.”
Then, Bentley is working with fellow UK company Fox Brothers to offer a Merino wool interior option, not just as a lesser-taken route for comfort (Volvo’s done well with wool, too) but also as a sturdy, renewable material that will hold up to automotive use. Finally, the assembly plant in Crewe, England, has tough requirements for green energy use (namely solar) and other renewable practices.
Output, battery, and charging specs are not carved into stone just yet. Power will be north of 800 hp and 700 lb ft of torque, and curb weight is estimated to be nearly 6,000 lbs. Page was quiet about battery size (though, expect it to mirror the Porsche’s 108 net kWh unit), and the targeted range is over 370 miles. With a peak charging rate of 400 kW, the brand is aiming for a 10–80 percent top-up in under 20 minutes, with 100 miles tacking on in as little as seven.
“We’re trying to be authentic in the whole experience,” Page summed up as we headed back to the parking lot where I met him.
The approach with the Torcal is to make a great Bentley first, and in the process of doing so, a great EV. It combines some already hashed-out tech from Volkswagen, but the brand is hoping its focus on craftsmanship and fine-tuning will attract discerning, well-heeled potential customers who want an electric luxury vehicle. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet, but it will be interesting to see how the Torcal is received after its full official unveiling.
Images by Bentley

articles.title: « Nous sommes entrés dans une nouvelle ère » : cette fusée réussit là où l'Europe attendait depuis des décennies
articles.text:
La deuxième fois était donc la bonne, et c’est une formidable avancée pour l’Europe spatiale. Samedi 5 septembre 2026, à 22h12, la fusée Spectrum de la société allemande Isar Aerospace s’est arrachée avec succès du pas de tir d’Andøya, tout au nord de la Norvège. Sept minutes plus tard, elle larguait ses satellites en orbite basse.
Le contraste avec le tout premier essai de l’entreprise est spectaculaire, et a de quoi faire sourire : en mars 2025, il y a à peine plus d’un an, cette même fusée retombait en mer au bout d’une trentaine de secondes, avant de s’abîmer dans une grosse explosion. Il y avait cependant quelques motifs de satisfaction : au moins, le lanceur avait décollé.
Cette fois, le scénario était différent : Isar Aerospace tient sa qualification, et l’Europe a surtout démontré qu’elle peut avoir un accès souverain à l’espace depuis son propre sol – plus exactement depuis l’Europe continentale, sans avoir besoin de recourir à une base spatiale lointaine, comme le centre spatial de Kourou, en Guyane française (Amérique du Sud).
Le lanceur Spectrum n’a pas la prétention de venir concurrencer Ariane 6. C’est un petit engin, haut de 28 mètres, large de 2 et mobilisant 10 moteurs pour emporter jusqu’à une tonne en orbite basse (entre 100 et 2 000 km d’altitude). C’est, en somme, un microlanceur, qui complète la gamme des fusées européennes sur un segment précis.
Ce vol, baptisé Onward and Upward, emportait en l’espèce cinq cubesats et une expérience, du matériel universitaire sélectionné par l’agence spatiale allemande (DLR) et soutenu par le programme Boost ! de l’Agence spatiale européenne. Boost ! vise à soutenir les initiatives commerciales proposant des services de transport spatial.
Rien n’a été simple pour Isar Aerospace entre le raté du printemps 2025 et le tir réussi de cette fin d’été 2026. Le premier vol avait donc tourné court et il fallait déjà se remettre en selle pour la suite. Ce rebond, d’abord espéré pour janvier, a hélas glissé de report en report. Le deuxième tir a connu une fuite dans un réservoir sous pression puis divers soucis.
Une réussite qui tombe à pic pour l’Europe
Hasard du calendrier, la fusée Spectrum est parvenue à décoller quatre jours avant un sommet spatial organisé à Paris par Emmanuel Macron, consacré à la souveraineté spatiale européenne – les 9 et 10 septembre 2026. Selon Les Echos, Washington a fait pression sur les géants comme SpaceX et Blue Origin pour qu’ils esquivent l’évènement.
Malgré cette manœuvre qui a poussé les entreprises américaines à déserter la séquence, des dizaines d’autres nations demeurent invitées et prévoient de venir. Surtout, l’Europe peut bomber le torse malgré le coup américain, et démontrer que l’on peut aussi se débrouiller sur le Vieux Continent. Même s’il aura fallu cravacher 18 mois pour gommer 30 secondes d’échec.
Ce timing, personne ne l’avait scénarisé. Mais la politique a évidemment saisi la balle au bond : pendant que Washington boude une conférence sur la gouvernance de l’orbite, Emmanuel Macron a salué le tir, dans un tweet qui visait aussi à donner le change. « L’Europe prend son destin en main, y compris dans le domaine spatial », a-t-il écrit.
« Pour la première fois, un acteur privé européen a placé sa fusée en orbite après un lancement depuis le sol européen. […] Une victoire pour toute l’Europe. […] Ces succès disent ce dont notre continent est capable lorsqu’il innove, investit et assume son ambition : bâtir une Europe puissance, indépendante jusque dans l’espace », a-t-il ajouté.
D’autres félicitations sont venues d’ailleurs en Europe, mais aussi de Josef Aschbacher, le directeur de l’Agence spatiale européenne, qui s’était alarmé du déclin européen dans le spatial et de la nécessité de davantage compter sur soi-même pour les vols spatiaux. Le concurrent américain Rocket Lab a aussi adressé ses félicitations.
Un vol de qualification n’est pas encore une cadence industrielle. Isar affirme avoir déjà cinq Spectrum en production et vise à terme jusqu’à 40 fusées par an dans sa future usine près de Munich, avec un second pas de tir prévu au Canada. C’est un rythme bien plus soutenu qu’Ariane 6 ou Vega-C, les deux lanceurs stars de l’Europe.
« Nous avons réalisé en quelques années ce qui avait pris des décennies à l’industrie spatiale européenne. L’Europe dispose désormais d’un accès souverain à l’espace. Nous sommes entrés dans une nouvelle ère pour les vols spatiaux européens. », juge Daniel Metzler, CEO et cofondateur. Isar Aerospace doit désormais enchaîner les tirs pour transformer cette réussite unique en service commercial régulier.

articles.title: Trezor data breach impact now reaches 81,000 customers
articles.text:
Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Trezor says an August data breach at its shipping and logistics provider, ShipMonk, affects an additional 67,000 U.S. customers.
In total, the breach has affected 81,000 customers after Trezor initially disclosed on August 13 that attackers accessed the data of nearly 14,000 customers, including their full names, shipping addresses, email addresses, and phone numbers.
As the company explained at the time, the incident also affected customers in Brazil, Colombia, Italy, Portugal, Sweden, and the United Kingdom who received orders between May 10 and August 8, 2026.
On Friday, it published an update to confirm that the breach impact has expanded after ShipMonk failed to delete the exposed data from its systems as required by Trezor's contract and data policy.
"Another 67,000 customers from the US who ordered between November 2019 and August 2021 were affected, with their full details (name, email, phone number, shipping address, order number) exposed," Trezor said.
"Throughout our entire relationship with ShipMonk, we repeatedly requested and received written assurance confirming the deletion of the data, in line with our contract, data policy, and past communications. We are very disappointed that, despite receiving this confirmation, the data was not deleted in their systems."
The company added that the breach did not affect its operations or services, that its systems were not compromised, and that all Trezor devices are secure.
It also warned affected customers to be wary of any messages requesting personal information, as they may be targeted in phishing attacks.
"Be aware of the increased risk of phishing. The leaked information could be used for scam emails, fraudulent calls or letters, and could potentially expose affected individuals to physical security risks," Trezor said.
Metabase campaign linked to ShinyHunters extortion gang
While the company has yet to share how ShipMonk's systems were breached, breach notification emails sent to affected customers and seen by BleepingComputer said the attackers exploited a vulnerability in the third-party analytics platform Metabase.
As BleepingComputer previously reported, Metabase revealed that the threat actors exploited a critical SQL injection zero-day vulnerability to breach customer instances and carry out data theft attacks after gaining administrator access to the compromised instance.
BleepingComputer has also learned that ShipMonk has received extortion emails from the ShinyHunters extortion gang.
The list of affected companies in the Metabase campaign includes online form-building platform Tally and laptop maker Framework, which have also notified customers of data breaches after their instances were hijacked.
In January 2024, Trezor disclosed another data breach after threat actors compromised its third-party support ticketing portal and accessed data (e.g., names, usernames, and email addresses) from roughly 66,000 users.
This stolen data was later used in phishing attacks attempting to steal recipients' 24-word wallet recovery seeds.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Dyson unveils new range of robot vacuums, air purifiers, floor cleaners and hair care products - Tech Guide

Dyson has unveiled a range of products incorporating advanced intelligence to deliver a new level of performance including a new robot vacuums, air purifiers, floor cleaners and hair dryers and straighteners.
DYSON R3 ROBOT NUROVI SPOT AND SCRUB UV – TBC
The Dyson R3 NUROVI Spot and Scrub UV can detect stains by using UV light, AI vision, and green laser illumination.
You can identify around 200 types of household substances and objects and will clean repeatedly until those stains are gone.
It has 30,000 PA and 65% more suction pressure for powerful cleaning across both hard floors and carpets.
It is set for release in early 2027.
DYSON R2 NUROVIA WASH AND DRY – $1,449
The Dyson R2 debuts the new Dyson Reuleaux triangle pads, which maintain constant width and contact to get right into the corners.
This way the vacuum maximises edge and corner contact for improved coverage.
The cleaning is enhanced with 75-degree Celsius water heated at the dock, which helps with the removal of stubborn stains.
DYSON R1 NUROVI DRY – $949
This has the same twin capture technology as the R2, with 21,000 Pa suction, and shares the same side sweeper system with a webbed connector that controls the pressure and direction of the brushes.
DYSON W1 PENCIL WASH – TBC
Dyson’s floor care range now includes the W1 Pencil Wash, which has been upgraded to add a more absorbent roller and hygienic wash system.
It also has self-cleaning technology on the charging dock and maintains the same light and slim design for easy use to achieve maximum cleaning convenience.
It will be available in early 2027.
DYSON HUSHJET BIG AND QUIET PURE+ FORMALDEHYDE AIR PURIFIER – TBC
The largest model in the range and the most powerful purifier Dyson has produced, the HushJet Big and Quiet Cool Pure+ Formaldehyde air purifier can clean rooms quickly and project purified air up to 20m.
The HushJet nozzle drew its inspiration from aviation and applies aerospace principles to control airflow in the home.
Due for release in early 2027.
DYSON HUSHJET COOL PURE+ FORMALDEHYDE AIR PURIFIER – $999
This delivers powerful Purification but has a more compact format yet can still handle large spaces quickly without the need to step up to a full-scale system.
The Dyson HushJet Pure Cool+ Formaldehyde air purifier offers up to 3x more powerful purification than its predecessors.
It can project air far into the room for improved purification while cooling at the same time.
Will be available in October.
DYSON HUSHJET HOT COOL PURE+ AIR PURIFIER – TBC
This is a powerful three-in-one purifier that brings purification, along with heating and personal cooling, in one product.
It is designed to offer comfort year-round and can be used in spaces where thermal comfort and air quality need to work closely together.
Due for release in early 2027.
DYSON CORRALE COOLSHINE STRAIGHTENER – $499
The Dyson Corral Cool Shine straightener has reimagined hot plate styling and changes the way hair is straightened, shaped, and finished.
It has precision heat control, flexing plates, and active cooling to deliver glossy, sleek, and straight results with less heat damage.
DYSON AIRSMOOTH HOT BRUSH – $399
This is Dyson’s first dedicated hot air brush that has been designed to simplify everyday styling routines while still delivering stunning results.
The product incorporates Dyson’s pioneering airflow technology with Pivot Flex and anti-snag bristle technology, which allows users to style with ease and help create a natural blowout across all hair types.

articles.title: French Days – L'objectif Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 105mm f/1.4E ED à 1 761,75 € (-10%)
articles.text:
French Days – L'objectif Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 105mm f/1.4E ED à 1 761,75 € (-10%)
L'objectif Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 105mm f/1.4E ED passe sous les 1800 € chez Fnac.com soit une baisse d'environ 10% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Après les 24, 35, 50, 58 et 85 mm, l'AF-S Nikkor 105 mm f/1,4E ED rejoint le club de moins en moins fermé des optiques Nikkor FX (24 x 36) ouvrant à f/1,4. Cette focale dédiée au portrait s'adapte, bien sûr, sur un reflex DX (APS-C) sur lequel il cadrera comme un 150 mm (157,5 mm, pour être précis). Soulignons qu'il s'agit du seul 105 mm f/1,4 autofocus du marché, toutes montures confondues, à l'heure où nous publions ces lignes.
Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 105mm f/1.4E ED
- 
                            Ergonomie
                            
            
- 
                            En pratique
                            
            
- 
                            Performances optiques
                            
            
Points forts
- Bokeh sublime, avec beaucoup de caractère.
- Possibilité de jouer avec de très faibles profondeurs de champ.
- Très bonnes performances optiques dès f/4.
- Qualité de fabrication.
Points faibles
- AF globalement lent.
- Pas de stabilisation.
- Vignettage prononcé (mais est-ce un défaut sur ce genre d'objectif ?)
S'il arrive à Nikon, comme nombre de ses confrères, de proposer des objectifs impersonnels, ce n'est absolument pas le cas de cet AF-S Nikkor 105 mm f/1,4E ED. Le bokeh est magnifique, doux et onctueux juste ce qu'il faut, rehaussé d'un vignettage prononcé somme toute agréable. En fermant un peu, ce 105 mm devient très précis et pourra, à l'occasion, sortir des sentiers battus du portrait, exercice dans lequel il excelle. Bravo.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
En alternative
Sigma Art 85 mm f/1,4 DG HSM
- 
                            Ergonomie
                            
            
- 
                            En pratique
                            
            
- 
                            Performances optiques
                            
            
Une fois de plus, nous recommandons sans la moindre hésitation cette optique. Sigma signe de nouveau une optique de haut vol qui fera le bonheur des amoureux du portrait.
La qualité optique est remarquable, même si au final l'objectif manque un peu de caractère. Le niveau de piqué et l'homogénéité dès la plus grande ouverture sont simplement impressionnants. Le Sigma Art 85 mm f/1,4 DG HSM avale sans sourciller les 50 millions de pixels d'un EOS 5Ds R et est donc prêt pour les générations futures de capteurs. La firme se paye même le luxe de parfaitement maîtriser le vignetage, si bien que certains fans des cadrages fermés devront en rajouter en post-production. L'objectif en lui-même jouit d'une excellente qualité de fabrication et d'une très bonne prise en main. Seul bémol : le poids et l'encombrement de l'objet ! Si vous comptez faire de longues séances à main levée, prenez bien en compte ce paramètre.
Sigma fait l'impasse sur la stabilisation optique, qui peut être un réel plus pour ce type de focale et une utilisation à main levée. La firme a privilégié avant tout la qualité optique sur cet objectif. Cette absence est compensée (en partie) par une très généreuse ouverture maximale de f/1,4. La nouvelle motorisation AF est efficace : l'autofocus est rapide, réactif et précis.

articles.title: Ya no es que los trenes no lleguen a su hora en Alemania, es que 400 personas quedaron atrapadas en un túnel seis horas
articles.text:
Vivimos de mitos y relatos que muchas veces no se ajustan a la realidad. Por ejemplo, a Alemania le ha tocado durante mucho tiempo convivir con una percepción exterior donde sus ciudadanos son muy trabajadores, incluso más que el resto de Europa (aunque los datos digan otra cosa). También que son la nación de las salchichas, la cerveza y la legendaria puntualidad de sus trenes. Y tampoco.
El derrumbe de un mito. Sí, durante décadas, Alemania cultivó la imagen de un país donde la puntualidad ferroviaria era tan parte de la identidad nacional como la cerveza o las salchichas. Hoy esa imagen se resquebraja: solo en torno al 60-61% de los trenes de larga distancia llega dentro del margen oficial de seis minutos, una caída notable respecto al 85% de los años noventa.
La situación se ha vuelto tan grave que Suiza ha vetado el paso de trenes alemanes más allá de Basilea, harta de los retrasos que afectan a su propia red. Casos como el de un tren averiado cerca de Viena que dejó a 400 pasajeros atrapados durante seis horas en un túnel, o el cierre durante nueve meses de la línea Berlín-Hamburgo para reparaciones desde agosto de 2025 (reabierto por completo el pasado 14 de junio), reflejan el colapso de un sistema castigado por tres décadas de infrafinanciación.
Entre el desgaste y la frustración. La compañía ferroviaria reconoce que el 80% de las demoras se debe a una infraestructura obsoleta, propensa a fallos y sobrecargada, lo que obliga a soluciones drásticas y a una costosa modernización. Para los pasajeros, la experiencia se ha vuelto un calvario cotidiano: esperas interminables, trenes abarrotados y conexiones perdidas que alteran tanto la vida profesional como la personal.
Viajeros como el banquero Michael Prieggen o el jubilado Gerald Vogel lo resumen en el Washington Post sin rodeos: la fiabilidad es ya la excepción, y la red se encuentra en estado de “desastre”. En estaciones como Wuppertal o Bonn, los retrasos se acumulan y las quejas se convierten en un coro de indignación que expresa una crisis de confianza en uno de los símbolos de la eficiencia alemana.
Promesas de inversión. ¿Soluciones? Ante este escenario, el gobierno ha destinado cifras récord: 25.000 millones de dólares en 2025 y más de 116.000 millones hasta 2029, con parte de los fondos procedentes de un paquete histórico de inversión en infraestructuras y clima que supone un cambio de rumbo en la disciplina fiscal germana.
El ministro de Transporte, Patrick Schnieder, calificó los niveles de puntualidad como “inaceptables” y prometió el año pasado mejoras sustanciales para alcanzar un 75-80% de trenes puntuales en 2027 (Schnieder dejó el cargo a finales de julio de 2026, en medio de una remodelación de gobierno de Merz, y Steffen Bilger fue propuesto como sustituto, con juramento previsto para el 9 de septiembre). Sin embargo, expertos y asociaciones de usuarios advierten de que el agujero creado por treinta años de abandono no se solucionará en pocos años y que la red requiere aún mayores inyecciones de capital y reformas estructurales. Plus: el objetivo se ha rebajado al 70% y aplazado hasta 2029.
Identidad nacional. Plus: la crisis ferroviaria alemana no es solo un problema de movilidad. Como decíamos, toca fibras sensibles de la identidad nacional. En un país donde la precisión y la fiabilidad se consideran virtudes colectivas, ver cómo el sistema ferroviario se derrumba o incluso se compara con otras naciones, resulta profundamente humillante. Que los suizos (referentes en eficiencia ferroviaria) desconfíen de los trenes alemanes es un golpe simbólico aún mayor.
Si se quiere, el debate trasciende lo técnico y refleja una ansiedad más amplia sobre la capacidad de Alemania para mantener el prestigio de su modelo económico y social. Los retrasos y averías, repetidos a diario, no solo obstaculizan viajes, sino que erosionan la confianza en la nación que antaño fue sinónimo de puntualidad mecánica.
Europa calienta. Es la última de las patas a analizar. El estado actual de Deutsche Bahn es tanto una crisis operativa como un más que posible espejo de los dilemas europeos: infraestructuras que envejecen, inversión insuficiente y una creciente tensión entre expectativas nacionales y realidades económicas.
No es solo que el viejo continente no esté preparado para una guerra debido a sus vías, es que Alemania, antaño ejemplo de modernidad ferroviaria, se ha convertido en un anuncio para navegantes. La nación se encuentra atrapada entre el recuerdo de su perfección pasada y la urgencia de reconstruir un sistema que ha dejado de cumplir con el ideal germano de puntualidad.
En esa brecha se juega no solo la credibilidad de una empresa, sino parte de la propia identidad del país, con Europa en el fondo del marco.
Una versión de este artículo se publicó en agosto de 2025

articles.title: No necesitas un Nokia 1100: Juega Snake II al estilo retro desde cualquier celular
articles.text:
El interés por el Nokia 1100 persiste más de dos décadas después de su lanzamiento. Su menú simple, la pantalla monocromática y los juegos preinstalados forman parte de una experiencia que hoy puede recuperarse sin conservar el dispositivo original.
Snake II puede jugarse desde un celular moderno o un navegador, mediante aplicaciones que recrean el teléfono clásico y versiones web desarrolladas en HTML5. Por esta razón, se explica todo lo que se debe saber para jugar este popular título de forma fácil y sin virus.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué aplicaciones permiten jugar Snake II en Android y iOS
Los teléfonos actuales ofrecen distintas opciones para acceder a Snake II sin recurrir al modelo de 2003. En las tiendas de Android y iOS hay emuladores y aplicaciones inspiradas en los celulares Nokia, con interfaces que recuperan el aspecto de los menús, los botones y los sonidos de aquella etapa.
Una de las aplicaciones más conocidas es Brick 1100, que busca replicar la apariencia del aparato, incluidos la linterna y los tonos característicos. Otra alternativa es Snake Game Classic Retro, centrada en la partida y en un sistema de control que intenta trasladar a la pantalla táctil la lógica del teclado numérico.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo jugar Snake II desde el navegador sin instalar una aplicación
Las versiones web son una vía directa para jugar desde un smartphone, una tableta o una computadora. Solo con escribir términos como “Snake II HTML5” en un buscador para encontrar remakes que funcionan desde el navegador y que imitan la pantalla verde, los píxeles oscuros y la cuadrícula que distinguieron al juego original.
Esta modalidad evita descargas, permisos y espacio de almacenamiento. Algunas páginas adaptan los controles a flechas en pantalla, mientras que otras permiten usar el teclado físico de una computadora.
PUBLICIDAD
El resultado varía según cada desarrollo, pero la mecánica se mantiene: guiar a la serpiente, recoger elementos y evitar que choque contra los bordes o contra su propio recorrido.
Qué otros juegos marcaron tendencia en la telefonía retro
Aunque Snake II concentra la mayor parte de la nostalgia, Space Impact+ fue el otro juego preinstalado del Nokia 1100. Adaptó los shooters espaciales a una pantalla reducida y a un teclado numérico, con enemigos, obstáculos y disparos que exigían avanzar por niveles sin perder las vidas disponibles.
PUBLICIDAD
El atractivo actual de ambos juegos está ligado a reglas simples y partidas breves. Un Nokia 1100 en funcionamiento, una aplicación para Android o iOS y un remake en HTML5 permiten acceder a esa experiencia sin las exigencias habituales de los smartphones.
Cómo jugar Snake II desde un Nokia 1100 original
Conseguir un Nokia 1100 sigue siendo posible en mercados de segunda mano, tiendas de artículos usados y plataformas de subastas. El teléfono puede conservar sus funciones básicas, aunque la mayoría de los países ya dejó atrás las redes 2G, así que es difícil o imposible utilizarlo para llamadas, mensajes de texto u otras funciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Esa limitación no afecta los títulos incluidos de fábrica. Snake II y Space Impact+ funcionan sin tarjeta SIM ni acceso a una red telefónica, de modo que el dispositivo puede utilizarse como una consola portátil.
Asimismo, para quienes buscan repetir partidas durante varias horas, el teléfono conserva una ventaja frente a otros teléfonos antiguos: sus juegos consumen pocos recursos.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué se debe revisar antes de comprar un teléfono usado
El punto principal es la batería. Muchos de estos modelos utilizan la BL-5C, una batería extraíble que todavía aparece en comercios especializados y sitios de reventa.
Conviene comprobar que el teléfono encienda, que el teclado responda sin demoras y que la pantalla no presente fallas, porque los controles numéricos son parte central de la jugabilidad.

articles.title: Ola Electric clears Rs 1,500 Cr fundraise; Startup funding dips marginally
articles.text:
Ola Electric clears Rs 1,500 Cr fundraise; Startup funding dips marginally
Ola Electric’s board approved a fund raise of up to Rs 1,500 crore, while Shradha Sharma and Manoj Kumar Kohli were approved for re-appointment as independent directors.
Dear Reader,
OpenAI has acknowledged a “wiki incident” in which its AI agents hijacked a community-edited German website and used it as a message board for cheating during tests and other rogue behaviour.
The company said the episode highlights the need for greater transparency around unintended AI behaviour, or “misalignment”, and admitted that the industry lacks clear standards for reporting such incidents. OpenAI is working with regulators worldwide on improving disclosure practices, following growing scrutiny over the safety of autonomous AI agents.
Meanwhile, social media is giving books a new lease of life. Communities such as BookTok and Bookstagram are turning reading into a social activity, with readers and creators sharing reviews, recommendations, bookshelf tours and more. The trend has helped books go viral, brought new readers to the habit and, somewhat ironically, encouraged people to spend less time on their screens.
The IPO market is set for a busy week, with 11 companies looking to raise a combined Rs 7,055 crore between September 7 and 15. The lineup spans sectors from real estate and manufacturing to fintech and online rentals, with Rentomojo, Karamtara Engineering, and Kanohar Electricals among the larger issues. Of the Rs 7,055 crore being targeted, Rs 4,333 crore or 61%, is expected to come through offers for sale.

articles.title: J'ai vu le HoverAir Versa : l'étonnante caméra qui se transforme en drone en quelques secondes
articles.text:
C’est l’une des attractions qui fait s’arrêter les curieux dans les allées du salon. La marque HoverAir, à l’origine connue pour la conception de drones, a dévoilé un système modulaire assez inédit. Nous avons pu le voir en action et le manipuler un peu pour nous faire une première idée.
De la main aux airs en quelques secondes
Faut-il forcément choisir entre caméra de poche et mini-drone ? Plutôt que de choisir, le HoverAir Versa a décidé de faire les deux. L’appareil se présente d’abord comme une petite caméra stabilisée que l’on utilise simplement à la main, comme une caméra DJI ou Insta360. Une fois la prise de vue manuelle terminée, il suffit de placer le module sur un corps doté d’hélices.
La transition opère à ce moment-là et une fois la caméra fixée sur son socle, l’interface de l’écran bascule pour passer en mode drone. Il ne reste plus qu’à déplier l’armature de l’appareil et à lancer le vol.
Un suivi réactif et intuitif
Le petit drone démarre ensuite en appuyant sur un bouton de la caméra. L’ensemble est réactif et l’écran se montre agréable à utiliser. La démonstration sur le stand confirme l’aspect très visuel du produit, tandis que le drone décolle directement depuis la paume de la main de l’utilisateur.
En plein vol, l’appareil est capable d’accrocher une personne pour la suivre avec précision. Le retour est tout aussi fluide, puisque le drone vient se reposer de lui-même, directement dans la main.
Et sur le plan technique ?
Le HoverAir Versa prend la forme d’une caméra à stabilisateur 3 axes surmontée d’un écran OLED de 1,64 pouce et d’un capteur type 1/1,3 pouce. Le constructeur ne s’étend pas sur sa définition, mais promet la possibilité de capturer des clichés de 12 Mpx et surtout de filmer jusqu’en 4K à 60 i/s (sans HDR) ou en 4K à 30 i/s (avec HDR). Un zoom numérique x2 est de la partie.
Côté autonomie, elle varie en fonction du mode d’utilisation, allant de 180 minutes en mode caméra classique à 14 minutes lorsque le drone vole. Notons que l’appareil dispose d’une batterie amovible, ce qui est plutôt rare sur une caméra de poche (mais plus courant sur les drones).
La caméra affiche 163 grammes et les hélices ajoutent 67 g, pour un poids total de 230 g en mode drone. Il reste aussi sous la barre des 250 g, lui permettant d’échapper à la majorité des obligations réglementaires.
Prix et disponibilité
Ce concept hybride sera commercialisé au prix de 739 euros. C’est un tarif qui semble relativement correct au vu de la polyvalence de l’engin. Si le produit vous intéresse, il faudra patienter encore un peu, puisqu’il sera disponible dans le courant du mois d’octobre.
Pour l’heure, le HoverAir Vera est disponible en précommande sur Indiegogo jusqu’au 17 octobre 2026, avec des tarifs avantageux.

articles.title: Mi-laptop, mi-tablette, ce MSI Prestige 16 Flip AI+ avec écran OLED et Intel Core Ultra X9 s'allège de 400 € pendant les French Days — Frandroid
articles.text:
Présenté lors du CES 2026, l’ultraportable Prestige 16 Flip AI+ est l’une des dernières machines lancées par MSI, une marque bien connue pour ses PC gamers, mais qui conçoit aussi de très bons PC portables taillés pour les professionnels. L’atout majeur de ce Prestige 16 Flip AI+ ? Ses charnières rotatives à 360°, qui lui permettent de se transformer en tablette. Un laptop très polyvalent, donc, mais également très puissant grâce à son Intel Core Ultra X9, qui est affiché à -20 % pendant les French Days.
Les points forts du MSI Prestige 16 Flip AI+
- Des charnières rotatives à 360°
- Une dalle OLED 2,8K de 16 pouces
- Un Intel Core Ultra X9 + 32 Go de RAM + SSD de 1 To
Initialement affiché à 1 999,99 euros, le MSI Prestige 16 Flip AI+ est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 1 599,99 euros à la Fnac et chez Darty.
Un grand laptop 2-en-1
L’un des grands points forts du MSI Prestige 16 Flip AI+ est inscrit dans son nom : il s’agit là d’un PC portable 2-en-1 au format « flip », doté de charnières rotatives à 360° qui permettent de replier l’écran sur le châssis pour créer une tablette. De quoi autoriser différents usages, et même plaire aux créatifs qui pourraient dessiner bien plus facilement. D’ailleurs, ces derniers pourront se servir du stylet MSI Nano Pen fourni, lequel peut être inséré dans la rainure dédiée sur le châssis et être rechargé par le biais de deux ports Pogo classiques. Une configuration que nous avons beaucoup appréciée lors de notre test de la version 14 pouces.
Le MSI Prestige 16 Flip AI+ est aussi particulièrement léger (1,66 kg) et assez peu épais (11,9/13,9 mm) : on peut donc l’emporter partout sans difficulté. Côté connectique, vous avez un port HDMI 2.1, deux ports Thunderbolt 4, deux ports USB 3.2 Gen 2 et un port jack. Et côté écran, MSI n’a pas fait les choses à moitié : dalle OLED tactile 2,8K (2 880 x 1 800 pixels) de 16 pouces, fréquence de rafraîchissement variable de 48 à 120 Hz, couverture complète du DCI-P3… Bref, un écran qui devrait satisfaire aussi bien les professionnels travaillant sur des logiciels de bureautique ou consultant de longs PDF que les créatifs qui retouchent des photos.
Un combo puissant pour faire tourner la machine
Sous le capot, on trouve tout d’abord un Intel Core Ultra X9 388H, doté de 16 cœurs, cadencé à 2,1 GHz et pouvant turbo jusqu’à 5,1 GHz. Un processeur que l’on a déjà testé dans l’Asus Zenbook Duo de 2026, et qui nous a franchement bluffés. Ici, il est épaulé par 32 Go de RAM LPDDR5X (extensible jusqu’à 64 Go), qui permettent de garder plusieurs onglets et applications ouverts simultanément, tout en offrant une bonne fluidité dans les tâches du quotidien et les logiciels gourmands. Une puce graphique intégrée permet de son côté d’accélérer les tâches créatives, type retouche photo et montage vidéo.
Un SSD de 1 To complète le tout et permet au laptop d’être plus réactif, avec des démarrages et des chargements rapides, tout en mettant à disposition un grand espace de stockage. Côté autonomie, la marque promet que son PC portable peut tenir toute une journée. Notez que le chargeur n’est pas inclus et que MSI recommande un adaptateur secteur de 65 W minimum.
Nous n’avons pas testé ce modèle de 16 pouces, mais vous pouvez toujours lire notre test complet de la version 14 pouces, dotée d’une configuration légèrement différente.

articles.title: Après un premier échec, cette fusée européenne réussit enfin à atteindre l'orbite
articles.text:
La fusée Spectrum, construite par l’entreprise allemande Isar Aerospace, a rejoint l’orbite terrestre hier depuis la Norvège et a déployé plusieurs satellites. Ce deuxième vol de l’engin, après un échec en 2025, est la première mise en orbite réalisée par une entreprise privée depuis l’Europe continentale.
Décollée à 22h12 hier du complexe de lancement dédié d’Isar Aerospace à Andøya Space, dans le nord de la Norvège, la fusée Spectrum a dépassé son point de pression maximale, coupé son moteur principal puis largué son premier étage, comme prévu au bout de quelques minutes. Le deuxième étage a pris le relais et l’engin a franchi la ligne de Karman, à 100 kilomètres d’altitude, frontière conventionnelle de l’espace. Comme vous pouvez le voir dans la vidéo ci-dessous, il a ensuite largué sa coiffe, gagné la vitesse orbitale et achevé une manœuvre de circularisation avant de séparer ses charges utiles.
Ces dernières proviennent d’un concours de microlanceurs organisé par l’agence spatiale allemande DLR et financé par le programme Boost! De l'Agence spatiale européenne, ouvert aux écoles d’ingénieurs et aux jeunes entreprises. Isar Aerospace travaille désormais avec ses clients pour confirmer l’état de chaque satellite.
L’Agence spatiale européenne vient d’accorder 198 millions d’euros à Isar Aerospace
On vous en avait parlé en mars, une première fusée Spectrum avait perdu sa stabilité quelques secondes après son décollage depuis Andøya, avant de basculer et de retomber dans la mer, sans faire de victime.
Après cet échec, Isar Aerospace avait reporté à plusieurs reprises ce deuxième essai, d’abord prévu le 21 janvier, pour des raisons techniques et de sécurité, avant de se relever avec ce décollage réussi du 5 septembre. Neuf jours plus tôt, l’Agence spatiale européenne avait signé avec Isar Aerospace un contrat de 197,8 millions d’euros, dans le cadre de l’European Launcher Challenge.
Ce programme est doté au total de plus de 540 millions d’euros. Il finance aussi l’allemand Rocket Factory Augsburg à hauteur de 186,9 millions d’euros et l’espagnol PLD Space pour 158,9 millions d'euros, et la française MaiaSpace doit prochainement le rejoindre avec un quatrième dossier. L'agence ne débloque les fonds qu’au fil des jalons techniques franchis par chaque entreprise, car elle veut sécuriser son investissement tout en accélérant les calendriers industriels. Le versement de la première tranche était soumis à une réussite orbitale attendue avant fin 2027. Isar Aerospace a rempli cette condition avec plus d’un an d’avance.
En juin, le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz avait affirmé attendre ce lancement avec impatience, avant de se réjouir des débuts prochains de deux autres sociétés spatiales privées en Allemagne. Avant ce succès, relève notre confrère Le Monde, Donald Trump avait ébranlé la confiance de plusieurs pays européens, inquiets de leur dépendance à Washington pour l’accès à l’espace.
Isar Aerospace a levé 270 millions d’euros
En cette fin de printemps, Isar Aerospace avait bouclé un tour de table de série D de 270 millions d’euros. Les nouveaux investisseurs Island Green Capital et Molten Ventures avaient rejoint cette opération, aux côtés des habitués HV Capital, Lakestar, UVC Partners et de la banque publique allemande KfW Capital. « Nous allons maintenant nous concentrer sur l'augmentation rapide de la production de lanceurs, honorer nos commandes et répondre à la demande mondiale croissante », a déclaré Daniel Metzler, P-. D. G et cofondateur d’Isar Aerospace.
Les lanceurs Spectrum numérotés de 3 à 7 sont déjà en fabrication, et Isar Aerospace doit porter sa capacité à 40 exemplaires par an dans une nouvelle usine de 40 000 mètres carrés, où l’entreprise combine intégration verticale et automatisation poussée.
L’entreprise construit par ailleurs un second site de lancement en Nouvelle-Écosse, au Canada, en complément de la base norvégienne d’Andøya. Ces nouvelles installations doivent couvrir les orbites à inclinaison moyenne à élevée. Ces orbites servent à l’observation de la Terre et aux télécommunications.
